Exercise 1. Pieces: ⁧وافتتح رئيس البلدية أمس المكتبة الجديدة في الحي الشرقي⁩ (main) · ⁧التي تضم أكثر من خمسين ألف كتاب⁩ (relative) · ⁧وتوفر قاعات للدراسة مفتوحة حتى منتصف الليل⁩ (related coordination) · ⁧معربا عن أمله في أن⁩ … ( ḥāl) · ⁧فيما انتقد سكان الحي⁩ ... (contrast). The mayor inaugurated yesterday the new library in the East Quarter, which hosts more than fifty thousand books and offers studios open until midnight, hoping that it will become a cultural center for young people. The locals, on the other hand, criticized the three-year delay in the project. 2. a) It was decided (the parties agreed) to postpone the elections. · b) The two ministers discussed how to strengthen trade. · c) The company has announced that it will start producing electric cars. · d) The plan aims to reduce pollution and improve air quality. · e) The press release called for accelerated implementation of the reforms. · f) An agreement has been reached after lengthy negotiations. Note for the e): ⁧دعا إلى ضرورة⁩ ... is a frequent redundancy in the press (they invited to the need for... Exercise 3. a) The minister left the room angry (irritated). · b) The spokesperson said the company will compensate customers, and added that the service will return tomorrow. · c) The government, however, did not comment on the news. · d) The minister said that the ministry will open an investigation, adding that no negligence will be tolerated. ·
e) As far as prices are concerned, they will remain stable.

Exercise 5. a) The President arrived in Cairo on 12 October. · b) Exports have reached 3,7 billions of dollars. · c) Samira al-Khatib, professor of economics at Alexandria University, said that... · d) This year the Ramadan begins the 18 February. · e) The government has allocated 250 Millions of Egyptian pounds for the project. · f) The summit was held in Rabat, the capital of Morocco. Exercise 6. Accuracy: 1) ⁧لم تستبعد⁩ = "not excluded', not "not announced'; 2) ⁧مليارات⁩ = + = billion (EUR) not = million (EUR) 3) ⁧سنويا⁩ = ... per year, not per month. Return: 1) Ed has occurred that... (lime); 2) "and indicated the minister" (order of words and repetition of the subject); 3) a single heavy period bound by "ed" . Correction: The minister did not exclude an increase in the 10% electricity tariffs next year, noting that subsidies cost the State 4 billions of dollars a year. 7. a) Written translation · b) simultaneous interpretation · c) machine translation · d) the sworn translator (B2-05) · e) language review, proofreading · f) fidelity in surrender

Exercise 9. a) Phase 1: cultural news; sources: the minister (discourse), the director of the center, independent translators. Phase 2: first paragraph: main ( ⁧افتتح⁩ … « ⁧المركز الوطني للترجمة⁩ (') with maṣdar ( ⁧الذي يهدف إلى ترجمة⁩ ...), supplement ( ⁧بتمويل يبلغ⁩ …). Third paragraph: main ( ⁧ويضم المركز⁩ … ⁧فريقا⁩ ), engraved with ⁧تم⁩ + maṣdar ( ⁧الذي تم إنشاؤه بالتعاون مع⁩ ...), coordinated ( ⁧كما يتضمن برنامجا⁩ … ⁧وقسما⁩ …). Phase 3, an example translation: "The Minister of Culture inaugurated yesterday in the capital the "National Translation Centre," which aims to translate a thousand books per year from foreign languages to Arabic and vice versa, with a financing of twenty million dollars in five years. In his speech during the ceremony, the minister said that the center "will fill a great void in the Arabic library," stressing that the number of books translated each year into Arabic "is still much lower than the needs of the region." The Centre, born in collaboration with several universities, has a team of 150 translators and auditors; It also includes a training programme for young translators and a section dedicated to machine translation. The director explained that, in the first phase, priority will go to books of science and technology and contemporary Asian and Latin American novels never translated before into Arabic. However, some independent translators have expressed reservations about working conditions, considering that the proposed remuneration "is not adequate for the required commitment"; the director replied that the remuneration "will be revised after the first year." 4: check figures (thousand, twenty million, five years, 150), quotes, the degree of ... will be revised. b) Progress: good translations of simple journalistic and technical texts, useful to understand the general sense. Limits: absence of vowels (plus readings), dialects, long and ramified phrases, expressions with cultural or religious load. The real risk: blind trust in machine translation, because a mistake about a number or a denial can change the sense without anyone who does not know Arabic notice it. Model: draft machine, revision and final translator responsibility. Personal answer on the last question. Exercise 10. See example translation of the exercise 9 (a). The tutor evaluates with the address book.

Exercise 12. a) The meaning, through words: it translates what words do. Because it's a cast with four maṣdar Chain. The Arab journalist loves the maṣdar, Italian verbs. Do not translate words but what they do; do not add or remove anything from the meaning (freedom in form, fidelity in content). b) Scientific transliteration of a name into an article; the date of the egyra left without explanation; “billion” translated as “million”. In an article: simple and consistent form or transcription without diacriticals; in an internal report: the rules of the customer and the Arabic name in brackets at first occurrence. The Gregorian date is added or explained (it is the first day of Ramadan). Because it changes the news a thousand times. c) Leave the translation for one day; reread it as those who do not know Arabic and stop on strange phrases; go back to the original and check numbers, names and denials word by word. Who knows how to find their mistakes. Unit verification. 1. The bridge was inaugurated yesterday. · 2. The two sides discussed how to develop the reports. · 3. The Director announced the start of the project (that the project will begin). · 4. The minister, however, did not comment. · 5. The spokesperson said that... and added that................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................................ · 6. An agreement has been reached. · 7. The press release called for accelerated reforms. · 8. The delegation arrived on 3 August. · 9–10. ⁧لم يؤكد⁩ = ... not confirmed (not confirmed) ⁧ما زال جاريا⁩ = is still in progress (is not over) · 11. Returns: ... and indicated the official ... repeats the subject and follows the Arab order. · 12–

14. The official did not confirm the news, noting that the investigation is still ongoing. Example: Ministry announced a plan by 1,2 billions of pounds to renovate thirty schools, ensuring that jobs will end before the beginning of the school year. Parents, on the other hand, doubt that the deadline can be met.
